text.rasmi: Use a formal, respectful register of standard Swahili when addressing the reader, in tutorials and technical pages alike; no slang or Sheng.

style.loanwords_text: Translate crypto terms into clear Swahili where a natural equivalent is understood; keep English only where the terminology list below keeps it. The terminology list wins over this rule.
writing_rules: Translate the visible text of links too (for example [Viewing Keys](…) becomes [Funguo za kutazama](…)); keep only brand and product names and protected terms in English. Never put the English in brackets inside link text: "[Funguo za kutazama](…)", not "[Funguo za kutazama [viewing keys]](…)"; if needed, put the English after the link.

Use Swahili word order around names: the noun comes first, then "cha/ya/la/wa/za" and the name ("Kitabu cha Zebra", not "Zebra Kitabu"; "Sera ya Fedha ya Zcash", not "Zcash Sera ya Fedha"; "Maboresho ya Mtandao wa Zcash"). Names of organisations and community chapters stay as they are (Zcash Foundation, Zcash Brazil).
Give the English in brackets only once per term per page, at first use; do not stack two brackets on one phrase.
"Trustless" means "not needing trust" ("isiyohitaji kuaminiana"), never "untrustworthy" («isiyo na uaminifu»). "API calls" are «maombi ya API», not «simu».
